chapter: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
title: Muggsy Spanier punches Leonard Feather
summary: Hodes tells how Muggsy punched Feather at Nick's and chased him into a Greek restaurant. He lists others who laid hands on Feather.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: He punched Leonard out like that.
This is the story. Leonard came into Nick's, and Muggsy was playing there. And during intermission,

Muggsy walked up to him and started to tell him what he thought about him. And Feather reached in his pocket and pulled out some manuscripts. "But Muggsy, I came here to write and I love you and all." With that, he hit him, and Leonard ran. And he ran and Muggsy chased him. And ran around the block and saw a restaurant, a Greek restaurant, and ran in there and shut the door.

Well, the Greek -- you're not shutting my door during business hours. So somehow he saved Leonard's rear end and Muggsy let it go at that one punch. But the story is now going around the Village, amongst those guys, that that's what happened. But he wasn't the only one. Coleman Hawkins, I understand, grabbed him. Danny Alvin grabbed him. A bass player that went to jail because of pot, who played for this pianist whose father also played piano years ago.
Eddie Heywood. And I can't think of this bass player's name. He had a --
Simmons. They didn't draw the line.
